name: Alacalufe-Central
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Central Alakaluf; only early vocabularies (Marcel 1892; Skottsberg 1913; Borgatello 1928); no description that would cover stress

sources.citation: Skottsberg, Carl. 1913. Observations on the natives of the Patagonian Channel region. American Anthropologist n.s. 15(4): 578-616 (vocabulary of c.301 words from the informant Emilia, Port Gallant area; JSTOR Early Journal Content via archive.org jstor-659721).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only a phonetic key (p. 606) that ends "' = principal: = secondary stress."; every vocabulary entry is marked for principal (and often secondary) stress (a'kwa:, ta'ju, kje'lu, i'rk'stakwarrR..), and p. 605 notes 'different individuals have a somewhat different pronunciation'. No statement of where stress falls.

sources.citation: Viegas Barros, Jose Pedro. 1990. Dialectologia qawasqar. Amerindia 15. Paris: A.E.A.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Defines the 'variedad Centro' (C) = Strait of Magellan vocabularies (La Guilbaudiere, Fenton/Cyrille in Hyades 1891, Skottsberg 1913 'un vocabulario C tipico', Borgatello 1928, c.750 lexical items); sections 3.4-3.5 give segmental system and N:C:S correspondences only; no mention of acento.

sources.citation: Gusinde, Martin. 1926. Das Lautsystem der feuerlaendischen Sprachen. Anthropos 21(5-6): 1000-1024; section II 'Das Lautsystem der Halakwulup', pp. 1010-1017 (archive.org anthropos_september-december-1926_21_5-6).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Segment inventory (vowels, diphthongs, consonants, glottalized stops) re-notating Skottsberg 1913 in the Anthropos alphabet with Gusinde's own 1923-24 examples; 'betont/unbetont' used only when describing vowel qualities (e.g. e 'tritt fast nur als unbetonter Vokal auf'); p. 1012 impressionistic remark on articulation 'ohne besondere Betonung des einen oder anderen [Lautes]'. No rule for word-stress placement. Gusinde's informants were from the Munoz Gamero / Skyring area, which Viegas Barros 1990 treats as a N-C transition zone rather than variety C proper.

sources.citation: Lehmann-Nitsche, Robert. 1921 (dated 1919). El grupo linguistico alakaluf de los canales magallanicos. Revista del Museo de La Plata 25: 15-69 (archive.org scanned of the tome).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative vocabulary; describes Borgatello's list (via Cojazzi 1911, c.550 words + 137 phrases, informant probably from around Dawson Island); a full-text search for stress/accent the article for acento/prosodia finds nothing on accent.

sources.citation: Cooper, John M. 1917. Analytical and critical bibliography of the tribes of Tierra del Fuego and adjacent territory. BAE Bulletin 63. Washington: GPO (archive.org scanned text).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 10 'Nothing has thus far been published on Alacalufan grammar'; the comparative glossary preface reproduces Skottsberg's key including "(') = principal stress; (:) = secondary stress (Skottsberg, d, 606, 614)"; no rule.

sources.citation: Skottsberg, Carl. 1915. Some additional notes on the language of the natives in the Patagonian Channels. American Anthropologist n.s. 17(2): 411-413 (archive.org jstor-660367).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparison with Coppinger's Tilly Bay list plus errata to the 1913 vocabulary; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hyades, Paul & Joseph Deniker. 1891. Mission scientifique du Cap Horn 1882-1883, t. VII, ch. 'Langage', pp. 272-279 (Fenton's Punta Arenas 'Alakalouf' list = variety C per Viegas Barros 1990).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlists with apostrophe marks on some words (tcharkoug, chalk'iki); no statement about accent (a full-text search for stress/accent tonique/accentuation in the language chapter: none).

sources.citation: Borgatello, Maggiorino. 1928. Notizie grammaticali e glossario della lingua degli indi Alakaluf abitanti dei canali magellanici della Terra del Fuoco. Torino: Societa Editrice Internazionale. 62 pp. (OCLC 1372222)

sources.note: The only grammar sketch Glottolog lists for alac1240 (703-word glossary with 'fonetizacion' per Viegas Barros 1990 plus grammatical notes); an Italian missionary sketch of this kind is the one place a remark on 'accento' could exist. HathiTrust bib API confirms Full view (rights pdus), Cornell copy.
